name: Crewmeister
description: Crewmeister, German time tracking, absence planning and shift planning for small businesses: members, teams and roles, absences and leave balances, clock stamps, durations, overtime balances, working time models, shifts, templates and workplaces. API v3 with a login token.
instructions:
**Credentials**: Crewmeister API v3 signs in with the e-mail address and password of a Crewmeister user. AnythingMCP posts them to `/api/v3/auth/user/`, receives a JWT and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer` on every call; it logs in again on its own when the token expires. Use a dedicated user (for example an admin account created for the integration) rather than a personal one: the API returns exactly what that user may see, so an ordinary member sees only their own data, while a crew owner or manager sees the whole crew or their teams. Single sign-on accounts without a Crewmeister password cannot log in here.

**Where to start**: `crewmeister_list_members` gives every person's `userId` (the id all other tools filter on) and `crewmeister_list_crews` the `crewId`. Then `crewmeister_list_absence_types` maps absence type ids to names.

**Mandatory filters**: five resources are computed per crew and date and answer 400 without them: `crewmeister_list_durations` and `crewmeister_list_calendar_days` need `crewId==<id>` plus a date or date range, `crewmeister_list_duration_balances` and `crewmeister_list_entitlement_balances` need `crewId==<id>;date==<day>`, and `crewmeister_list_absence_entitlements` needs `crewId==<id>`. Ranges such as `crewId=gt=0` are not accepted there.

**Filtering (RSQL)**: every list tool takes `filter`, an RSQL expression. Use `==`, `!=`, `=lt=`, `=le=`, `=gt=`, `=ge=`, `=in=(1,2)`; join conditions with `;` (AND) or `,` (OR); `*` is a wildcard in string values. Examples: `userId==123;date=ge=2026-09-01;date=le=2026-09-30` for one person's month, `state==REQUESTED` for open absence requests. Dates are `yyyy-MM-dd`; timestamps are ISO 8601 with an offset. A filter on a field the resource does not support answers 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT.

**Paging**: pages start at 0 and hold 20 items by default (`page_size` to change). The answer has `content`, `totalElements`, `totalPages` and `hasNextPage`; call again with `page` + 1 while `hasNextPage` is true. `sort` takes keys such as `+from` or `-timestamp`.

**Which time data to use**: stamps are the raw clock-in and clock-out events, bookings are the processed time entries, durations the per-day totals by type (WORK, BREAK, OVERTIME), and duration balances the running overtime account. For "hours worked last month" use durations; for "who is clocked in now" use stamps of today.

**Absences** move through DRAFT, REQUESTED, PRE_APPROVED, APPROVED, REJECTED and REVOKED. Remaining vacation is in `crewmeister_list_entitlement_balances` (filter userId and a date).

**Secrets are left out**: the crew's join password and members' terminal PIN codes are removed from the answers.

**Errors**: 401 means the login failed or the token was refused; 403 PERMISSION_DENIED and 404 NOT_FOUND also cover records the user may not see. Reading with a filter the user may not see returns an empty page rather than an error.

The v2 API was retired on 31 March 2026; this connector uses v3 only.
prerequisites: A Crewmeister user with an e-mail address and password (not single sign-on). The connector sees what that user may see, so use a crew owner or manager account for company-wide data.

CREWMEISTER_EMAIL.label: Login e-mail
CREWMEISTER_EMAIL.help: The e-mail address you sign in to app.crewmeister.com with. Use an account with manager or owner rights for the whole crew.
CREWMEISTER_EMAIL.patternMessage: The e-mail address of the Crewmeister login.

CREWMEISTER_PASSWORD.label: Password
CREWMEISTER_PASSWORD.help: The password of that Crewmeister login. Reset it at app.crewmeister.com if the account uses single sign-on only.

verifyHints.400: Crewmeister did not accept the login (it answers 400 "User not found" for an unknown e-mail or a wrong password). Check that you can sign in at app.crewmeister.com with the same e-mail and password.
verifyHints.401: Crewmeister refused the token issued for this login. Check that you can sign in at app.crewmeister.com with them, and that the account is not single sign-on only.
verifyHints.403: The login works but this user may not read this data. Use an account with manager or owner rights.

tools.name: crewmeister_list_members
tools.description: List the members (employees) of the crew with id, userId, name, e-mail, employee id, first and last working day and disabled flag. The userId here is the id every other tool filters on.

filter.description: RSQL filter. Operators: == != =lt= =le= =gt= =ge= =in=(a,b) =out=(a,b); join with ; for AND and , for OR. Dates are yyyy-MM-dd, timestamps ISO 8601 with offset. Fields: id, crewId, userId, name, email, username, employeeId, employeeType, disabled, firstWorkingDay, lastWorkingDay. Example: disabled==false;name==*Müller*

sort.description: Sort keys, each a field name with + (ascending) or - (descending) in front, e.g. ["+name"].

page_size.description: Items per page. Default 20; ask for up to 100 at a time.

tools.name: crewmeister_get_member
tools.description: Return one member by its member id with name, e-mail, userId, employee id, language, working-day range and disabled flag.

id.description: Member id (the id field from crewmeister_list_members, not the userId).

tools.name: crewmeister_create_stamp

timestamp.description: When the event happened, ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-10-06T08:00:00+02:00.

tools.name: crewmeister_create_absence
tools.description: Create an absence for a user: a request (state REQUESTED) that a manager approves, or, for managers, an approved entry. Dates and type cannot be changed afterwards.
